Test_Name: Advective flux vs boundary migration independence
Scheme_Component: Fixed-Grid Eulerian transport (Steps 4-5) vs flotation remapping (Steps 7-8)
Potential_Double_Count_Mechanism: Q_GL (ice advection through fixed face) and Delta_M_boundary (domain volume change from x_GL shift) might both appear to represent mass leaving the grounded domain — but be counted separately
Formal_Proof_That_Double_Count_Does_NOT_: Q_GL = W_GL * H_GL * u_GL is computed from ICE VELOCITY u_GL at the fixed grounding-line face. Delta_M_boundary = rho_i * W_GL * H_GL * v_GL * Delta_t is computed from BOUNDARY VELOCITY v_GL = dx_GL/dt. These are physically distinct: u_GL is the ice flow through the face; v_GL is the geometric movement of the face itself. The continuous Reynolds Transport Theorem explicitly separates these two contributions: dM_gr/dt = Mdot_SMB - rho_i * Q_GL + Mdot_boundary.
Mathematical_Identity: Q_GL = W_GL * H_GL * u_GL [ADVECTION]; Q_boundary = W_GL * H_GL * v_GL [BOUNDARY MIGRATION]; Q_relative = Q_GL - Q_boundary = W_GL * H_GL * (u_GL - v_GL) [NET ICE FLUX ENTERING OCEAN]. In the Fixed-Grid Eulerian scheme: Q_GL appears in Step 5d (applied as FV outflow boundary condition); Delta_M_boundary appears in Step 8 (derived from x_GL change). They are SUMMED in the diagnostic residual identity — not the prognostic update. No single physical quantity is counted twice.
Status: PASS — no double counting by construction of the Fixed-Grid Eulerian scheme

Test_Name: Eulerian transport uses fixed-face outflux only
Scheme_Component: Steps 5c-5d: Eulerian FV on FIXED grid cells. No mesh velocity term.
Potential_Double_Count_Mechanism: A moving-mesh (ALE) scheme would add a mesh-velocity term to the advective flux equation. If both fixed-face advection AND a mesh-velocity term were included the boundary migration would be counted twice.
Formal_Proof_That_Double_Count_Does_NOT_: The planned scheme is EXPLICITLY Fixed-Grid Eulerian (not ALE). Steps 5c-5d use standard upwind FV: H_i^(n+1,*) = H_i^n + (Delta_t/(W_i*Delta_x)) * [Q_{i-1/2} - Q_{i+1/2} + S_i]. There is NO mesh-velocity term in this equation. The mesh does not move. Therefore no ALE mesh-velocity contribution is present to double-count.
Mathematical_Identity: Proof by construction: the FV stencil in Steps 5c-5d contains ZERO terms involving v_GL or dx_GL/dt. The term Delta_M_boundary is first computed in Step 8 — after transport is complete — and appears ONLY in the diagnostic residual, not in the prognostic thickness update.
Status: PASS — ALE mesh-velocity term is explicitly absent from the prognostic update

Test_Name: Flotation remapping changes domain designation only — not thickness
Scheme_Component: Steps 7a-7b: flotation test reclassifies cells from grounded to floating (or vice versa). This changes g(n+1) and lambda_g^(n+1).
Potential_Double_Count_Mechanism: The flotation remapping might be mistaken for a second mass-removal step if interpreted as subtracting ice that was already removed by Q_GL in Step 5d.
Formal_Proof_That_Double_Count_Does_NOT_: Steps 7a-7b apply the flotation criterion to the intermediate field H^(n+1,*) which is the result of Eulerian transport. They do NOT modify H^(n+1,*). They only update the Boolean grounded mask and the boundary position x_GL^(n+1). The mass redistribution (Steps 9a-9c) then accounts for the reclassification. At no point is H_i^(n+1,*) reduced a second time for the same flux that Q_GL already removed.
Mathematical_Identity: Proof by enumeration: H_i^(n+1) is set once in Steps 5c-5d. It is not modified in Steps 7-9. Steps 9a-9c only update the LEDGER (grounded vs floating accounting) based on how many cells changed grounding status — they do not reduce H_i^(n+1) further.
Status: PASS — flotation remapping is a domain-reclassification operation

Test_Name: Retreat bookkeeping does not re-subtract Q_GL flux
Scheme_Component: Steps 9a-9b transfer mass from grounded to floating ledger when x_GL retreats.
Potential_Double_Count_Mechanism: The ungrounded mass Delta_M_unground might appear to double-subtract the mass that was already reduced in H_g by Q_GL in Step 5d.
Formal_Proof_That_Double_Count_Does_NOT_: Q_GL in Step 5d reduces H_g^(n+1,*) compared to H_g^n by the amount of ice that FLOWED OUT through the grounding-line face during Delta_t. The retreat bookkeeping in Steps 9a-9b identifies ice that remains in the cell but is now RECLASSIFIED as floating because the grounding line has retreated upstream of that ice. These are different ice parcels: Q_GL removes ice that crossed the face; retreat bookkeeping reclassifies ice that never left the cell but is now floating.
Mathematical_Identity: Proof by physical interpretation: H_g^(n+1,*) already reflects the outflow of Q_GL. The ice remaining in the cell (rho_i * W_g * H_g^(n+1,*) * lambda_g^(n+1,residual) * Delta_x) is distinct from the Q_GL outflow. Delta_M_unground = rho_i * W_g * H_g^(n+1,*) * (lambda_g^n - lambda_g^(n+1)) * Delta_x refers only to the REMAINING ice, not to the already-evacuated flux.
Status: PASS — Q_GL and Delta_M_unground are mutually exclusive mass parcels

Test_Name: Advance bookkeeping does not re-add previously-counted floating ice
Scheme_Component: Steps 9c add Delta_M_ground to the grounded ledger from the floating reservoir when x_GL advances.
Potential_Double_Count_Mechanism: Floating ice being regrounded might have already been counted in Mdot_SMB or some other source term.
Formal_Proof_That_Double_Count_Does_NOT_: Mdot_SMB represents surface mass balance — precipitation minus ablation on ice surfaces. It does NOT include floating ice that reclassifies to grounded. Delta_M_ground in Step 9c is sourced EXCLUSIVELY from the floating ledger (or BedMachine initial state for cells not yet visited), which tracks floating ice that was previously ungrounded. The SMB and floating-regrounding terms act on entirely different mass reservoirs.
Mathematical_Identity: Proof by budget construction: Mdot_SMB^n = rho_i * sum_i(S_i^n) where S_i is the SMB rate applied to the ice surface. It is summed in Step 6 from the SMB field — no floating-ledger mass appears in Mdot_SMB. The floating ledger is a separate accounting ledger updated only by Steps 9a-9c (retreat/advance). Zero overlap.
Status: PASS — Mdot_SMB and floating-to-grounded reclassification are mutually exclusive

Test_Name: Diagnostic residual uses all four terms without internal cancellation
Scheme_Component: Diagnostic: Delta_M_cons = M_gr(t_{n+1}) - M_gr(t_n) - Delta_t*Mdot_SMB + Delta_t*rho_i*Q_GL - Delta_M_boundary
Potential_Double_Count_Mechanism: The residual itself might combine overlapping terms, making it appear zero by cancellation of errors rather than by true conservation.
Formal_Proof_That_Double_Count_Does_NOT_: The four terms in the residual arise from DISTINCT physical mechanisms: (1) M_gr change: direct cell-volume summation; (2) Mdot_SMB: surface accumulation from SMB field; (3) rho_i*Q_GL: advective mass outflux through GL face; (4) Delta_M_boundary: geometric boundary migration. These four terms are computed from independent data paths. If any single physical process were counted in two terms simultaneously the residual would equal zero for the wrong reason. The double-counting proof (DC_01 through DC_05) demonstrates each process appears in exactly one term.
Mathematical_Identity: Proof by exhaustive enumeration: every mass-affecting process in the timestep maps to exactly one residual term: SMB -> Mdot_SMB; GL advection -> rho_i*Q_GL; boundary migration -> Delta_M_boundary; residual net change -> M_gr(t_{n+1})-M_gr(t_n). No process appears in more than one term.
Status: PASS — all four residual terms are orthogonal; zero residual is a genuine conservation test
